classification.difficultyReason: Requires converting equal opposite-side vectors into equal position vectors for the diagonal midpoints.

content.prompt: Prove, using vectors, that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

spec.description: Oblique parallelogram ABCD with both diagonals and an unlabelled intersection. Source blue has no mathematical distinction and is replaced by house black; boundary strokes remain heavier than diagonals.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a parallelogram; AC and DB cross. No numerical dimensions, midpoint marks or origin are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete source figure is visible with the question.

answer.short: The diagonal midpoints have position vectors $\frac12(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{c})$ and $\frac12(\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{d})$. These are equal because $\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}=\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{d}$. Thus the diagonals share their midpoint and bisect each other.
